text: Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer. When a program doesn't work as expected, the first step is identifying the bug. This means carefully reading error messages and checking which part of the code causes the problem. Instead of guessing, it's wise to use a systematic approach. Many developers use debugging tools, like breakpoints, which pause the program at specific lines so you can inspect variable values. Another helpful strategy is logging. By adding print statements or log messages, you can track the flow of execution and see where things go wrong. Remember, patience and a clear method are often more valuable than making random changes to fix a stubborn error.
